phases.name: Freeze the brief and define forecast evaluation
phases.description: Preserve the stated 90-day accuracy and 25% savings goals as test criteria while identifying missing workload, history, and cost-baseline definitions.

phases.name: Collect multi-cloud capacity and cost evidence
phases.description: Ingest provider inventory and billing data, normalize a broad resource catalog, retain time-series history, and produce versioned forecasts.

phases.name: Turn forecasts into reviewable actions
phases.description: Model scenarios, bottlenecks, instance choices, and commitment plans; generate reports and alerts; measure outcomes without silently changing production capacity.

steps.phase: Freeze the brief and define forecast evaluation
steps.title: Start from the frozen capacity-planning problem
steps.content: Problem: Design an Intelligent Capacity Planning System (aiops_007; design-an-intelligent-capacity-planning-system). Category: AIOps - Capacity Planning; domain: aiml; difficulty: Hard; estimated time: 60-90 minutes. Description: Design an AI-driven capacity planning system that forecasts future resource needs, models growth scenarios, optimizes cloud spending, and provides procurement recommendations. Requirements: Forecast resource utilization trends; Model multiple growth scenarios (base, high, low); Identify capacity bottlenecks before they occur; Optimize instance types and sizing; Support reserved instance and savings plan planning; Generate capacity reports for leadership; Handle multi-cloud capacity views; Alert on resources approaching capacity limits. Constraints: Forecast accuracy within 10% for 90-day horizon; Support 1000+ resource types across services; Update forecasts daily; Reduce over-provisioning by 25%; Handle seasonal and event-driven patterns. Supplied hints include time-series decomposition, simulation, instance optimization, what-if analysis, cloud billing APIs, and saturation detection. Companies named in the frozen row: Netflix, Amazon, Google, and Densify; these are context, not required vendors.

steps.phase: Freeze the brief and define forecast evaluation
steps.title: Keep accuracy and savings definitions testable
steps.content: The problem does not specify forecast granularity, metric units, sampling interval, missing-data policy, history length, provider inventory cadence, service coverage, currency/discount treatment, or how the 25% over-provisioning reduction is calculated. Define the 10% error metric per resource class and horizon before selecting a model; aggregate accuracy can hide failures in low-volume services. Treat daily updates as a freshness objective, not an exact schedule guarantee. Savings-plan and reserved-instance advice should be recommendations with a human approval step unless the product later authorizes automated purchases or resizing.

steps.phase: Freeze the brief and define forecast evaluation
steps.title: Separate forecasts from production changes
steps.content: Use the system to recommend and explain capacity actions, but keep actual resizing and commitment purchases behind existing approval and execution workflows. The brief asks for optimization and procurement recommendations; it does not authorize automatic production changes.

decision.question: Should the planner directly resize resources or purchase commitments?
decision.chosen: Generate versioned recommendations and reports for an authorized human or existing deployment workflow to approve.
decision.chosenReason: This satisfies planning and optimization goals while keeping an auditable boundary around high-impact cost and availability changes.

alternatives.option: Automatically resize or purchase from each forecast
alternatives.tradeoff: Could reduce manual effort, but forecast error or stale pricing could cause outages or unwanted spend; the brief provides no authority or safety policy for automation.
Safer but fails to address instance sizing, commitment planning, and actionable capacity optimization.

steps.phase: Collect multi-cloud capacity and cost evidence
steps.title: Give operators one multi-cloud planning surface
steps.content: Show fleet coverage, forecast confidence, scenarios, resource-level bottlenecks, cost assumptions, and pending recommendations. Let leadership reports preserve their input-data and model versions so numbers are explainable later.

component.label: Capacity Planning Console

properties.purpose: Present multi-cloud fleet coverage, base/high/low forecasts, bottleneck evidence, cost assumptions, and versioned recommendations to operators and leadership.

component.highlightReason: A common operator surface makes cross-cloud comparison and reviewable recommendations part of the design.

steps.phase: Collect multi-cloud capacity and cost evidence
steps.title: Expose a versioned planning API
steps.content: Validate tenant, cloud scope, resource filters, scenario parameters, and report requests. Keep planning reads separate from any eventual execution API so recommendation generation cannot mutate infrastructure by accident.

component.label: Capacity Planning API

properties.purpose: Validate planning and reporting requests, apply tenant-aware admission, and route read-only forecast/recommendation operations separately from any future execution workflow.

component.highlightReason: A bounded API creates a clear trust boundary for multi-cloud data and cost recommendations.

steps.phase: Collect multi-cloud capacity and cost evidence
steps.title: Scope provider credentials and tenant visibility
steps.content: Authorize each operator and service against the tenant's connected accounts and permitted resource scopes. Keep provider credentials in an external secrets facility and use least-privilege read access for inventory and billing collection.

component.label: Tenant & Cloud Account Authorization

properties.purpose: Authorize tenant users and collection services for explicitly connected cloud accounts and permitted inventory, usage, and billing scopes.

component.highlightReason: Multi-cloud visibility depends on safe account scoping; credentials and recommendations must not cross tenant boundaries.

steps.phase: Collect multi-cloud capacity and cost evidence
steps.title: Compare scenarios and explain recommendations
steps.content: Combine forecasts with provider instance catalogs, current utilization, pricing, commitments, and operator constraints. Show why a recommendation fits and which uncertainty could change it; do not optimize solely for lowest nominal cost if availability or performance constraints are unknown.

component.label: Scenario & Rightsizing Engine

properties.purpose: Evaluate base/high/low growth scenarios, detect projected bottlenecks, compare instance sizes and commitment options, and emit explainable recommendations for approval.

component.highlightReason: Forecasting becomes useful when scenario outputs are translated into transparent sizing and procurement choices.

steps.phase: Collect multi-cloud capacity and cost evidence
steps.title: Schedule durable daily refresh and scenario jobs
steps.content: Use durable jobs for daily collection/forecast refreshes and operator-requested scenario runs. Preserve input-window and model versions for retries, and prevent a delayed provider API from producing a silently partial forecast.

component.label: Collection & Forecast Job Queue

properties.purpose: Buffer idempotent daily collection, normalization, forecast, and scenario jobs; expose retries and partial-source status instead of treating a missing provider response as zero usage.

component.highlightReason: Durable job state makes the daily freshness objective observable and recoverable.

steps.phase: Collect multi-cloud capacity and cost evidence
steps.title: Normalize provider inventory and billing feeds
steps.content: Implement provider-specific adapters behind one normalized resource model. Collect inventory, utilization, billing, instance catalogs, and commitment data with source timestamps and quality flags; the 1000+ resource-type target requires coverage tracking and schema evolution.

component.label: Multi-Cloud Inventory & Billing Adapters

properties.purpose: Use provider-specific read-only adapters to collect resource inventory, utilization, pricing, billing, and commitment data, then normalize schemas with source timestamps and coverage status.

component.highlightReason: Provider adapters are the replaceable seam that makes a unified multi-cloud view possible without assuming identical cloud APIs.

steps.phase: Collect multi-cloud capacity and cost evidence
steps.title: Maintain resource identity and type coverage
steps.content: Store canonical resource identity, provider-specific type mapping, region/account, ownership, sizing options, and commitment state. Track unmapped or unsupported types explicitly so the planner does not imply full coverage where adapters are incomplete.

component.label: Resource Catalog & Commitment State

properties.purpose: Store normalized resource identities, provider type mappings, account/region ownership, available sizing options, and current reserved-instance or savings-plan state.

component.highlightReason: The system must reason across 1000+ resource types and compare recommendations with current commitments.

steps.phase: Collect multi-cloud capacity and cost evidence
steps.title: Keep timestamped utilization history
steps.content: Retain timestamped measurements and their source/quality metadata for trend, seasonality, and event-aware forecasts. History duration and sampling interval are not specified; determine them from forecast validation and provider data limits rather than inventing a fixed retention period.

component.label: Timestamped Utilization Series

properties.purpose: Store timestamped utilization and cost series with source, unit, completeness, and quality metadata for forecasting and later accuracy evaluation.

component.highlightReason: Trend, seasonality, and daily forecast refresh require queryable historical measurements with trustworthy timestamps.

steps.phase: Collect multi-cloud capacity and cost evidence
steps.title: Preserve auditable source snapshots
steps.content: Keep raw or compacted source snapshots and forecast inputs only as long as needed for reproducibility and policy. This supports backtesting and explains provider-data gaps; the brief does not set a retention period.

component.label: Forecast Inputs & Audit History

properties.purpose: Retain policy-controlled source snapshots, backtest inputs, and forecast artifacts with timestamps and model/data versions for reproducible review.

component.highlightReason: Forecast accuracy cannot be audited later unless the source windows and model versions can be reconstructed.

steps.phase: Collect multi-cloud capacity and cost evidence
steps.title: Forecast per resource class with uncertainty
steps.content: Forecast utilization at an agreed resource and metric granularity, include seasonality and known events where data supports them, and expose confidence or data-quality warnings. The 10% error target over 90 days is a validation criterion, not an assumed model guarantee.

component.label: Resource Demand Forecaster

properties.purpose: Generate versioned resource-utilization forecasts with uncertainty and data-quality metadata, using trend, seasonal, and supported event signals.

component.highlightReason: A 90-day forecast target needs a measurable, versioned model output rather than a one-time static recommendation.

steps.phase: Collect multi-cloud capacity and cost evidence
steps.title: Generate comparable leadership reports
steps.content: Aggregate forecasts, scenarios, risks, coverage gaps, costs, and recommendation status into reports with clear assumptions and provenance. Keep uncertainty visible rather than presenting a single precise-looking number.

component.label: Capacity & Cost Reporting

properties.purpose: Produce leadership reports comparing scenarios, forecast confidence, bottlenecks, cloud coverage, costs, and approved recommendations with data/model provenance.

component.highlightReason: Leadership reporting is a functional requirement and should expose assumptions and uncertainty, not just totals.

steps.phase: Collect multi-cloud capacity and cost evidence
steps.title: Notify owners before projected capacity limits
steps.content: Route alerts with the affected resource, forecast window, confidence, owner, and supporting evidence. Define alert thresholds with operators; the problem does not prescribe a lead time or severity policy.

component.label: Capacity Risk Notifications

properties.purpose: Notify resource owners of approaching capacity risks with forecast horizon, confidence, resource identity, and an auditable link to the underlying recommendation.

component.highlightReason: Bottleneck detection only helps if a responsible owner receives an actionable, explainable warning.

steps.phase: Collect multi-cloud capacity and cost evidence
steps.title: Observe collection freshness and model error
steps.content: Track provider coverage, source age, missing metrics, forecast error by horizon/resource class, queue delay, scenario execution, and realized recommendation outcomes. Do not declare daily refresh complete when a provider source failed or coverage shrank.

component.label: Forecast & Collection Health

properties.purpose: Measure provider coverage and freshness, missing data, forecast error by resource/horizon, job delay, scenario runs, and realized outcomes.

component.highlightReason: Daily refresh, forecast accuracy, broad resource coverage, and over-provisioning reduction all require ongoing measurement.

steps.title: Connect the operator surface to planning APIs
steps.content: Send scenario, report, and recommendation requests through the versioned API. Return the data window and model version used so users can compare results over time.

connection.label: Scenario, forecast & report requests
connection.description: Operators request scoped forecasts, what-if scenarios, recommendations, and provenance-rich reports.

steps.title: Authorize cloud account and tenant scope
steps.content: Resolve the user and connected-account scope before returning inventory, cost, or recommendation details. Keep provider credentials out of the browser and report payloads.

connection.label: Tenant & connected-account authorization
connection.description: Check the caller's tenant, cloud accounts, and permitted inventory or billing scope before reading planning data.

steps.title: Run only authorized planning requests
steps.content: Pass the authorized scope and policy to the scenario engine. Recommendations remain read-only outputs until an explicitly approved execution system accepts them.

connection.label: Authorized planning scope
connection.description: Invoke scenario and sizing analysis using only the caller's permitted account, resource, and policy scope.

steps.title: Compare against current resource and commitment state
steps.content: Read normalized resource types, current sizes, provider availability, ownership, pricing references, and existing commitments. A recommendation must include the source and timestamp of any price or type catalog used.

connection.label: Resource types, sizes & commitments
connection.description: Read normalized inventory, sizing choices, account mappings, and commitment state for multi-cloud comparison.

steps.title: Request daily refreshes and bounded scenario runs
steps.content: Enqueue refresh work idempotently and report per-provider completion. Operator what-if jobs should not replace the scheduled daily run or overwrite the forecast version being reviewed.

connection.label: Daily refresh & scenario jobs
connection.description: Durably enqueue scheduled collection/forecast work and separately identified operator what-if runs.

steps.title: Collect data through provider adapters
steps.content: Workers call read-only cloud inventory and billing APIs, use backoff for provider throttling, and mark incomplete accounts explicitly rather than filling missing values with zero.

connection.label: Idempotent provider collection jobs
connection.description: Dispatch scheduled and operator-triggered collection work to provider adapters with retry and partial-source status.

steps.title: Normalize resource types and cost references
steps.content: Map provider-specific schemas to canonical resource identity and units; preserve the original provider type and mapping version for traceability. Track coverage toward 1000+ types as an explicit test matrix.

connection.label: Normalized inventory & pricing catalog
connection.description: Persist provider/type mappings, resource identity, sizing options, and timestamped cost and commitment references.

steps.title: Append quality-tagged utilization observations
steps.content: Store observations with event time, collection time, unit, source, and completeness markers. Delayed or missing samples must remain visible to forecasting and accuracy evaluation.

connection.label: Timestamped usage and cost observations
connection.description: Append normalized measurements with source time, collection time, units, and quality/completeness metadata.

steps.title: Preserve reproducible forecast inputs
steps.content: Record the source window, schema/mapping versions, and collection gaps used for each run. Choose retention after privacy, audit, and backtesting requirements are established.

connection.label: Versioned source snapshots
connection.description: Retain policy-controlled raw or compacted inputs and data-quality provenance for reproducible backtests.

steps.title: Forecast trends and event-aware utilization
steps.content: Supply historical series with resource and quality metadata. Evaluate multiple horizons through day 90, compare seasonal/event-aware and simpler baselines, and surface confidence and drift to downstream decisions.

connection.label: Historical utilization series
connection.description: Provide timestamped, quality-tagged resource history for trend, seasonal, event, and forecast-horizon evaluation.

steps.title: Use snapshots for backtesting and seasonality
steps.content: Backtest against time-correct historical snapshots and known events to avoid look-ahead leakage. The required history window is a product decision tied to the 90-day evaluation and should be measured against data availability.

connection.label: Backtest windows & known events
connection.description: Provide versioned historical windows and event annotations for leakage-safe backtesting and reproducible model evaluation.

steps.title: Associate forecasts with current resource identity
steps.content: Join time series to normalized resource type, provider, region, and current sizing. This allows accuracy and bottleneck results to be segmented by resource class and cloud rather than hidden in one aggregate.

connection.label: Resource identity & type features
connection.description: Join measurements to canonical provider, resource-type, region, ownership, and sizing metadata.

steps.title: Feed versioned forecasts into scenario analysis
steps.content: Pass forecast distributions, confidence, model version, and data-quality warnings to the optimizer. Keep the base forecast distinct from high/low growth scenarios so scenario assumptions are not mistaken for model output.

connection.label: Forecasts, confidence & provenance
connection.description: Provide versioned utilization forecasts and data-quality/confidence metadata for scenario and bottleneck analysis.

steps.title: Publish explainable scenarios and cost recommendations
steps.content: Report base/high/low outcomes, projected saturation, sizing alternatives, commitment options, cost assumptions, and approval state. Highlight when confidence or resource coverage is insufficient for a recommendation.

connection.label: Scenario results & reviewable recommendations
connection.description: Send explainable scenarios, bottlenecks, sizing/commitment alternatives, assumptions, and approval state to reporting.

steps.title: Return provenance-rich reports to operators
steps.content: Render leadership summaries alongside resource-level evidence, confidence, provider coverage, data window, and model version. Keep recommendations traceable to their inputs and approval history.

connection.label: Reports, coverage & recommendation status
connection.description: Present versioned reports and actionable recommendations with their assumptions and evidence.

steps.title: Alert owners about forecast capacity risk
steps.content: Send an alert only when the forecast crosses an operator-defined capacity policy and include confidence, expected horizon, and the next review action. Do not invent a lead-time threshold absent from the brief.

connection.label: Evidence-backed capacity risk alerts
connection.description: Notify owners about projected saturation with forecast horizon, confidence, resource identity, and policy context.

steps.title: Track multi-cloud collection coverage
steps.content: Measure connector success, provider throttling, unmapped resource types, source age, and partial account coverage. The daily refresh is not complete until freshness and coverage are reported per source.

connection.label: Provider coverage & collection freshness
connection.description: Report source freshness, API errors/throttling, type-mapping coverage, and partial collection status.

steps.title: Evaluate forecast error at each horizon
steps.content: Compare forecasts with subsequently observed values using the agreed per-class error metric. Alert on drift or missing inputs; do not interpret a single overall accuracy score as proof of 90-day performance.

connection.label: Horizon-specific forecast and drift metrics
connection.description: Export versioned predictions and later actuals for segmented accuracy, drift, seasonality, and event-impact evaluation.

steps.title: Measure recommendation adoption and realized savings
steps.content: Track whether recommendations were accepted, rejected, or deferred and compare realized utilization/cost against a defined baseline. Only then can the 25% over-provisioning reduction be evaluated without attributing unrelated spend changes to the planner.

connection.label: Recommendation decisions & realized outcomes
connection.description: Record approval outcomes and compare realized cost/utilization with an agreed baseline for savings evaluation.

steps.title: Close the loop on capacity alerts
steps.content: Track delivery, acknowledgement, and resolution outcomes for alerts so owners can tune noise and thresholds based on evidence rather than arbitrary defaults.

connection.label: Alert delivery & resolution outcomes
connection.description: Observe notification delivery and operator acknowledgement/resolution to refine capacity-risk alert policies.

steps.title: Validate the daily refresh and 90-day forecast
steps.content: Gate recommendations on complete provider coverage, fresh input windows, and validated accuracy. Backtest the 90-day horizon per resource class, exercise seasonal and event-driven periods, and evaluate the 25% reduction with an agreed baseline and adoption window.

scaleTrigger.metric: Forecast error by horizon/resource type, daily input freshness, supported type coverage, and measured over-provisioning outcome
scaleTrigger.action: Segment validation by provider, service, resource type, and event period; add adapter/model capacity only where measured coverage or forecast error fails the agreed criterion.
scaleTrigger.impact: The 10% accuracy, 1000+ types, daily update, 25% reduction, and seasonal/event-pattern constraints remain acceptance targets until this evidence exists.

steps.title: Keep procurement and resizing decisions auditable
steps.content: Use explainable, versioned recommendations and preserve approval outcomes. If an execution workflow is later added, define blast-radius limits, rollback, authorization, and budget guardrails as a separate product requirement.

decision.question: How should the system apply rightsizing and commitment recommendations?
decision.chosen: Keep recommendations read-only and require approval through the organization's existing change or procurement process.
decision.chosenReason: The brief asks for planning and recommendations but does not specify authorization for automatic infrastructure or purchasing actions.

alternatives.tradeoff: Could accelerate savings, but expands scope into production change and procurement risk not defined by the frozen requirements.
Avoids execution risk but leaves instance sizing and commitment planning unaddressed.
